answer: Staking is a concrete sybil defense: to vote or transact, every agent must lock a deposit it forfeits if caught coordinating fake identities or double-signing. A thousand sybils then cost a thousand real bonds, so the attack stops paying for itself. Reputation should melt like a glacier when fraud is proven — slow to build, quick to collapse — and a slashed identity stays marked across the horizon of later epochs. Cheap puppet accounts remain sable shadows at the edge of the market: visible, but powerless without capital truly at risk.
